title: UNDP Ethiopia Call for Proposals 2026: CSOs and NGOs for the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme to End Violence Against Women and Girls
summary: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Ethiopia has opened a Call for Proposals for Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and NGOs under the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 to End Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG) . The opportunity invites eligible civil society organizations to submit proposals for work connected to a major regional programme focused on addressing violence against women and girls. The assignment is structured as a CSO contract and is expected to run from November 2026 to December 2028 , with implementation described as home-based . The procurement notice, published by UNDP Ethiopia under reference UNDP-ETH-00793 , has an application deadline of 2 October 2026 at 04:00 AM New York time . Organizations interested in participating must use the UNDP Quantum supplier portal to access and submit their bids. Organizations that already have supplier profiles are instructed not to create duplicate accounts. Opportunity Overview The UNDP opportunity is connected to the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 , whose overarching focus is ending violence against women and girls (EVAWG) . The procurement notice identifies the following key details: Detail Information Organization United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Office UNDP Ethiopia Opportunity Call for Proposals – Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) or NGOs Programme Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 to End Violence Against Women and Girls Reference Number UNDP-ETH-00793 Contract Type Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) Duty Station Home-based Expected Duration November 2026 – December 2028 Expected Start Upon signing of the agreement Application Deadline 2 October 2026 at 04:00 AM New York time Contact EK or EW – info.procurementet@undp.org The notice was published on 18 September 2026 . What Is the Spotlight Initiative? The Spotlight Initiative is a global partnership involving the United Nations and the European Union that focuses on eliminating all forms of violence against women and girls. The initiative takes a broad approach to violence against women and girls, recognizing that meaningful progress requires action across areas such as policies, institutions, prevention, data, services, women s movements, and wider social systems. The Africa regional programme is designed to support regional commitments and address barriers that limit progress toward ending violence against women and girls. Previous Spotlight Initiative programming has been connected to issues including gender-based violence, harmful practices, sexual and reproductive health and rights, legislation, policies, data, and strengthening women s movements. The regional programme therefore provides a broader framework within which civil society organizations can contribute to efforts to prevent and eliminate violence against women and girls. What Is SIARP 2.0? The Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 represents the second phase of the Africa regional programme. The opportunity described in the UNDP procurement notice specifically identifies Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 to End Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG) as the service/work description. The programme s regional character is important because the initiative is not presented as a conventional local project limited to one community. It is connected to broader African efforts addressing violence against women and girls. For participating CSOs and NGOs, this creates an opportunity to contribute to a regional development agenda while working within the programme s specified objectives, requirements, and implementation framework. Why Civil Society Organizations Are Important Civil society organizations play an important role in addressing violence against women and girls because they often work directly with affected communities and can provide perspectives that complement government and international institutions. Depending on the specific requirements contained in the solicitation documents, CSOs may contribute through activities such as: Community engagement Advocacy Awareness and prevention Women s rights programming Gender equality initiatives Evidence generation Capacity strengthening Coalition building Policy engagement Community-based interventions Support for women and girls Partnerships with regional and national stakeholders However, organizations should not assume that all of these activities are automatically eligible under this specific call. The final scope of work, deliverables, eligibility requirements, and evaluation criteria must be taken from the complete UNDP solicitation documents. Who Can Apply? The procurement notice specifically identifies Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and NGOs as the intended applicant/contracting category. This means the opportunity is designed for organizations rather than individuals seeking employment, scholarships, fellowships, or internships. Potential applicants should therefore have an organizational structure capable of entering into an agreement with UNDP and delivering the services or activities required by the solicitation. Organizations should carefully examine the full procurement documents to determine whether they meet all applicable requirements concerning: Legal registration Organizational status Technical capacity Relevant experience Financial capacity Staffing Governance Previous project implementation Safeguarding Reporting Monitoring and evaluation Geographic coverage Compliance with UNDP requirements The excerpt provided in the procurement notice does not contain the complete eligibility criteria, so organizations should not rely solely on the summary information when determining their eligibility. Geographic Eligibility The opportunity is issued through UNDP Ethiopia , while the programme itself is identified as the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme . The notice therefore clearly connects the opportunity to an Africa-focused regional programme. However, the supplied procurement notice does not explicitly provide a complete list of eligible countries for CSO applicants. It would therefore be inappropriate to assume that every African organization automatically qualifies or that the opportunity is restricted exclusively to Ethiopian organizations. Organizations should review the complete solicitation documents available through the UNDP procurement system for the definitive geographic eligibility requirements. Contract Duration The expected implementation period is relatively long compared with many short-term NGO opportunities. The procurement notice states that the contract is expected to run from: November 2026 to December 2028 The expected start date is: Upon signing of the agreement. This means the successful organization should be prepared for a substantial period of engagement rather than a short-term activity. The actual commencement will depend on the completion of the procurement process and signing of the agreement. Duty Station and Working Arrangement The procurement notice identifies the duty station as: Home-based This indicates that the opportunity is not presented as a conventional office-based position at a UNDP location. Nevertheless, organizations should carefully examine the full solicitation documents because home-based does not necessarily mean that every activity can be undertaken remotely without any travel, meetings, field activities, consultations, or other forms of engagement. Any specific travel, geographical implementation, reporting, or coordination requirements should be confirmed from the complete solicitation documents. Application Deadline The deadline for this UNDP Call for Proposals is: 2 October 2026 at 04:00 AM New York time. Applicants should pay close attention to the time zone because the deadline is expressed in New York time , rather than Ethiopian local time or the applicant s own local time. Organizations should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their proposal. Online procurement systems can require account verification, document uploads, technical checks, and other steps that may take time to complete. Learn More and Apply HERE How the UNDP Supplier Portal Works One of the most important aspects of this opportunity is that applications are not submitted through an ordinary email application. The procurement notice states that the tender is managed through the new UNDP Quantum supplier portal system . Organizations interested in submitting a bid must therefore use the appropriate supplier portal process. UNDP provides specific instructions for both new and existing suppliers. Organizations Without a Supplier Profile Organizations that have never registered with the UNDP supplier system need to create a supplier profile through the designated registration process. Applicants should provide the required organizational information accurately and ensure that the organization s legal details correspond with its official registration and banking documentation. Organizations With an Existing Supplier Profile Organizations that already have a supplier profile should not create a new profile . Instead, they should log into the existing account and access the relevant procurement opportunity. The procurement notice specifically instructs existing suppliers to use the appropriate access route and search for the negotiation using reference number: UNDP-ETH-00793 This reference number is important because it allows applicants to identify the correct procurement opportunity within the supplier system. Important Supplier Registration Requirement The procurement notice contains an important instruction concerning the supplier name. When registering in the supplier portal, organizations should use their full legal name , matching the name used on their: Legal registration documents Bank account Official organizational records This is an important administrative requirement because inconsistencies between the supplier profile, legal identity, and banking information can create complications during procurement and contracting. Organizations should therefore ensure that their information is accurate before submitting their bid. What Applicants Should Do Before Submitting Organizations should begin by reviewing the full solicitation package rather than preparing a proposal based only on the summary procurement notice. The complete documents should be examined for information such as: Detailed scope of work Eligibility requirements Technical specifications Expected outputs Deliverables Evaluation criteria Financial requirements Proposal format Organizational documentation Submission instructions Contract conditions Monitoring and reporting requirements Safeguarding and compliance requirements Any geographic restrictions This is particularly important because the procurement notice itself provides only an overview of the opportunity. Drafting a Strong Organizational Proposal Organizations should ensure that their proposal responds directly to the requirements contained in the official solicitation documents. A strong proposal should generally demonstrate a clear understanding of: The problem being addressed The programme objectives The organization s proposed contribution The target groups or communities The implementation approach Expected results Organizational capacity Relevant previous experience Monitoring and evaluation Risk management Sustainability Financial requirements Applicants should avoid submitting a generic organizational profile without clearly demonstrating how their experience and capabilities correspond to the specific requirements of the UNDP solicitation. Demonstrating Relevant Experience Relevant organizational experience can be particularly important in competitive procurement processes. CSOs and NGOs should be prepared to demonstrate previous work related to areas relevant to the solicitation. Depending on the final requirements, useful evidence may include previous projects involving: Violence against women and girls Gender equality Women s rights Gender-based violence Protection and safeguarding Community mobilization Advocacy Policy engagement Research and evidence Capacity building Women s movements Sexual and reproductive health and rights Prevention of harmful practices Partnerships with governments or international organizations Organizations should only claim experience that they can substantiate through appropriate documentation. The Importance of Safeguarding Because the programme concerns violence against women and girls, organizations should pay particular attention to safeguarding and protection requirements contained in the full solicitation. Organizations working with vulnerable populations should have appropriate systems for: Preventing harm Protecting participants Managing sensitive information Handling complaints Responding to safeguarding concerns Maintaining confidentiality Ensuring staff accountability Protecting survivors and affected communities Any safeguarding requirements specified by UNDP should be addressed directly in the proposal and implementation plan. Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting Organizations participating in a UNDP-supported programme should expect accountability for results. Although the complete requirements must be taken from the solicitation documents, organizations should be prepared to demonstrate how they would: Track implementation Measure progress Document results Collect relevant data Report against agreed indicators Identify challenges Adapt implementation where appropriate Provide evidence of outputs and outcomes A credible monitoring and evaluation approach can help demonstrate that an organization understands not only what activities it proposes to conduct but also how it will determine whether those activities are producing meaningful results. UNDP Procurement Registration and Submission The procurement notice provides several important routes for accessing the opportunity. Applicants can use the UNDP Quantum supplier portal to search for the procurement opportunity. Organizations should search using the reference: UNDP-ETH-00793 Applicants should also subscribe to the tender within the procurement system. Subscribing is important because the procurement notice states that it allows the system to send notifications concerning amendments to the tender requirements . This is particularly important for organizations preparing their proposals over several days or weeks because procurement documents can potentially be amended before the deadline. What If an Organization Needs Clarification? The procurement notice provides a contact point for questions and clarification: EK or EW Email: info.procurementet@undp.org The notice also instructs suppliers to use the messaging functionality in the procurement system when further clarification is required. Organizations should use the official communication channels rather than relying on unofficial summaries or third-party information. What If an Organization Experiences Technical Problems? Organizations that encounter difficulties using the online procurement system should consult the relevant UNDP supplier guidance. The procurement notice directs applicants to UNDP s resources for bidders and indicates that organizations can seek support using the contact information associated with the tender. Applicants should resolve technical problems well before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours. Key Documents The procurement notice provides access to the relevant Negotiation Documents through the UNDP procurement system. These documents are particularly important because they contain the detailed requirements that applicants need to understand before submitting a proposal. Organizations should review the complete documentation rather than relying exclusively on the procurement notice s summary fields. Why This Opportunity Matters for African Civil Society Organizations The Spotlight Initiative s focus on ending violence against women and girls places the opportunity within a major development and gender-equality agenda. Violence against women and girls intersects with numerous social, economic, legal, health, and human-rights issues. Civil society organizations can provide important community-level knowledge and implementation capacity while also contributing to advocacy, evidence generation, accountability, and policy engagement. The regional nature of SIARP 2.0 also places the opportunity within a wider African context rather than limiting the programme s ambitions to a single community-level intervention. Important Distinction: This Is Not an Individual Job Opportunity Although the notice contains terms such as duty station and contract, this opportunity should not be confused with an individual UNDP employment vacancy. The procurement notice explicitly identifies the contract type as: Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) The intended applicants are therefore organizations capable of submitting institutional proposals and entering into an agreement with UNDP. Individuals seeking jobs, internships, scholarships, or fellowships should not treat this procurement notice as an individual employment opportunity. Key Facts at a Glance Organization: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Office: UNDP Ethiopia Reference: UNDP-ETH-00793 Opportunity type: Call for Proposals for CSOs/NGOs Programme: Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 Focus: Ending Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG) Contract type: Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) Duty station: Home-based Expected duration: November 2026 to December 2028 Expected start: Upon signing of the agreement Published: 18 September 2026 Deadline: 2 October 2026 at 04:00 AM New York time Submission system: UNDP Quantum supplier portal Tender reference: UNDP-ETH-00793 How to Apply Organizations interested in this opportunity should begin by accessing the UNDP procurement notice and reviewing the complete negotiation documents. The application process involves the following broad steps: Confirm organizational eligibility against the complete solicitation documents. Register as a UNDP supplier if the organization does not already have a supplier profile. Use the existing profile if the organization has previously registered with UNDP. Search for reference UNDP-ETH-00793 within the supplier portal. Review the complete solicitation and negotiation documents. Subscribe to the tender to receive notifications about amendments. Prepare the required technical and financial documentation. Follow all formatting and submission requirements. Submit the bid through the UNDP Quantum supplier portal. Complete the submission before 2 October 2026 at 04:00 AM New York time. Organizations should not create duplicate supplier accounts if they already have a registered UNDP profile. Visit HERE to learn more and apply for the UNDP Ethiopia Call for Proposals 2026. Pro Tip for Applicants Start with the full solicitation documents , not the summary notice. Before investing substantial time in proposal writing, verify that your organization satisfies the eligibility requirements and then map each proposal section directly against the evaluation criteria, scope of work, expected outputs, and submission instructions. Also subscribe to the tender in the supplier portal so that you receive notifications if UNDP issues amendments or clarifications before the deadline. Conclusion The UNDP Ethiopia Call for Proposals for Civil Society Organizations and NGOs under the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 provides an opportunity for eligible civil society organizations to contribute to regional efforts aimed at ending violence against women and girls. The opportunity is structured as a CSO procurement/contracting opportunity , rather than an individual employment programme. Successful organizations are expected to work under an agreement beginning around November 2026 and continuing through December 2028 , with the procurement notice identifying the duty station as home-based. The most important immediate consideration for interested organizations is the 2 October 2026 deadline at 04:00 AM New York time . Because submissions must be made through the UNDP Quantum supplier portal , organizations should not wait until the deadline to resolve registration, account-access, document-upload, or technical issues. Organizations should also remember that the information contained in the summary procurement notice is not a substitute for the full solicitation package. The complete documents should be used to confirm eligibility, geographic requirements, technical specifications, deliverables, evaluation criteria, financial requirements, and all other conditions of participation. For organizations working in areas related to women s rights, gender equality, violence prevention, protection, advocacy, community engagement, and related fields, careful review of the full solicitation documents will be essential before deciding whether to submit a proposal. Application Deadline: 2 October 2026 at 04:00 AM New York time. Reference Number: UNDP-ETH-00793 Discover more global Grant and African opportunities on OFY. title: Internet Society Fellowship Program 2027: $5,000 Project Stipend, Mentorship and Global Internet Leadership Opportunity
summary: The Internet Society Fellowship Program 2027 is a global fellowship opportunity for Internet changemakers, emerging leaders, practitioners, and professionals who want to develop practical solutions to Internet-related challenges in their communities and contribute to a stronger, more open, secure, trustworthy, and globally connected Internet. The redesigned 10-month Internet Society Fellowship Program combines self-paced pre-fellowship training, leadership development, specialized learning, mentorship, project development, practical project implementation, expert engagement, and participation in relevant Internet community events. Selected fellows receive a project stipend of up to US$5,000 , subject to submission and approval of a project budget, as well as travel support to attend a relevant global or regional Internet event. Fellows also gain access to a global network of Internet leaders and the Internet Society Alumni Network. The 2027 program is expected to welcome 90 fellows across three major tracks: Internet Policy and Mobilization, Internet Connectivity, and Internet Safety and Security. Unlike a conventional fellowship in which candidates submit an application immediately, the Internet Society has introduced a two-stage pathway. Prospective fellows must first complete the required Pre-Fellowship Training and develop a realistic project plan. Only after successfully completing the required training do participants become eligible to apply for the Fellowship Program. The training enrollment period runs from 23 September 2026 to 22 November 2026 , while fellowship applications close on 18 December 2026 . Applications become available on a rolling basis once eligible trainees complete the required modules. About the Internet Society Fellowship Program The Internet Society Fellowship Program is designed to develop people who can translate knowledge and ideas into practical action. The Internet Society describes the program as a structured learning and leadership experience combining: Pre-fellowship training Foundational Internet and leadership learning Track-specific learning Mentorship Practical project development Project implementation Expert engagement Participation in relevant Internet community events Networking with Internet leaders The central idea is that fellows should not simply learn about Internet-related challenges. They should use the knowledge, skills, networks, mentorship, and resources gained through the program to develop and implement a practical project that addresses a real-world challenge. The Fellowship Project is therefore a central component of the program. Each fellow is expected to design and implement a project that advances the Internet in their community, country, region, or area of expertise. The new model brings together learning and development opportunities that were previously offered through separate Internet Society fellowship programs. The Internet Society says the redesigned structure creates a more connected experience covering learning, mentorship, project implementation, event participation, and cross-disciplinary collaboration. What Makes the Internet Society Fellowship Different? One of the most important features of the current program is that participants do not immediately apply for the fellowship. Instead, the process begins with a free Pre-Fellowship Training and project-planning experience . During approximately 2.5 months of training, participants: Select a fellowship track and sub-track. Complete the required learning modules. Develop their knowledge of the Internet ecosystem. Explore a specific Internet-related problem. Develop a practical project idea. Build a realistic project plan. Complete the required training. Receive access to the fellowship application once eligible. Completing the training does not guarantee selection as a fellow. The Internet Society explains that fellowship selection is competitive and considers factors including the quality, feasibility, relevance, alignment, and potential impact of the proposed project. The training itself provides value even to participants who are not eventually selected. The Internet Society states that people who complete the training receive specialized knowledge, a certificate of completion, and a practical project plan that they can continue developing independently or use for a future application. Fellowship Tracks and Sub-Tracks The program is organized around three major tracks, each with two specialized sub-tracks. 1. Internet Policy and Mobilization This track is designed for people working to influence Internet policy and mobilize communities around Internet-related issues. It includes two sub-tracks: Internet Policy Community Mobilization The Internet Policy sub-track can be relevant to people interested in Internet governance, policy development, digital rights, regulation, and related policy questions. The Community Mobilization sub-track focuses on engaging communities and building support for Internet-related initiatives. The broader track is intended to develop advocates capable of connecting policy and community action with local Internet challenges. 2. Internet Connectivity The Internet Connectivity track focuses on technical and community-oriented approaches to expanding Internet access and strengthening Internet infrastructure. Its two sub-tracks are: Peering Community-Centered Connectivity The track is designed to build technical champions working in areas such as community networks, peering, Internet infrastructure, and connectivity planning. The official track information indicates that applicants take foundational Internet courses as well as specialized courses connected to their selected sub-track. 3. Internet Safety and Security The Internet Safety and Security track focuses on strengthening the security, trustworthiness, and safety of the Internet. Its two sub-tracks are: Systems Security Online Trust and Safety This track can be particularly relevant to people working in cybersecurity, online safety, security research, digital trust, and related areas. The program seeks to develop cybersecurity researchers and online safety champions capable of applying their expertise to practical Internet challenges. Fellowship Benefits Successful fellows receive several forms of support throughout the program. Project Stipend of Up to US$5,000 Selected fellows can receive a project stipend of up to US$5,000 , subject to submission and approval of their project budget. The funding is connected to the practical fellowship project and is intended to provide resources for fellows to implement their proposed initiatives. Applicants should therefore develop realistic projects with clearly defined objectives, activities, deliverables, and intended outcomes. The Internet Society emphasizes that fellows receive project support through mentorship, expert guidance, structured reporting, and project funding. Dedicated Mentorship Each fellow receives a dedicated mentor aligned with their project area and selected fellowship track or sub-track. Mentorship provides an opportunity for fellows to receive guidance as they develop and implement their projects. This is particularly relevant because the fellowship project is expected to move beyond a theoretical idea into an achievable intervention with measurable outputs. Travel Support Selected fellows receive travel support to attend a relevant global or regional Internet event . The Internet Society gives examples such as: Internet Governance Forum (IGF) Africa Peering and Interconnection Forum (AfPIF) NDSS Symposium Other events relevant to the fellow s program track The specific event opportunities can vary according to the fellow s track and program priorities. Global Internet Leadership Network Fellows have the opportunity to connect with a global community of Internet leaders. The program is designed to create relationships among people working across different areas of the Internet ecosystem, including policy, technology, civil society, community development, security, and connectivity. Internet Society Alumni Network After completing the fellowship, participants gain access to the Internet Society Alumni Network . The alumni network provides an opportunity to remain connected with other people who have participated in Internet Society programs and to continue sharing knowledge, expertise, and professional relationships. The Fellowship Project The practical project is one of the most important components of the fellowship. Every fellow is expected to develop and implement a project that advances the Internet in their: Community Country Region Area of expertise The project is implemented over six months and serves as the main practical component of the fellowship. It enables fellows to apply the knowledge, skills, and networks developed throughout the program to a real-world Internet challenge. Projects are expected to have: Clear objectives Defined activities Specific deliverables Intended outcomes A realistic implementation plan Potential for meaningful impact Potential outputs can include: Policy briefs Research reports Training programs Community engagement initiatives Workshops Technical resources Implementation plans Awareness campaigns Toolkits Operational guides Other tangible resources that contribute to a stronger Internet The Internet Society encourages applicants to select a project category that best aligns with their proposed work. Program Learning Modules The fellowship includes a foundational leadership component as well as specialized learning. The foundational leadership core includes: Introduction to the Internet Society The Internet ecosystem Leadership Project management Advocacy Communications Participants also undertake expert sessions related to their selected sub-track and participate in mentor check-ins. This combination is intended to ensure that fellows develop not only technical or policy expertise but also the leadership and project-management capabilities needed to turn their ideas into practical results. Pre-Fellowship Training The Pre-Fellowship Training is a compulsory part of the application pathway. It consists of self-paced online learning designed to prepare prospective fellows for the full fellowship experience. The Internet Society states that participants should expect to dedicate approximately 30 hours to the training, excluding the additional time required to develop their proposed project. The training period for the current cycle runs from: 23 September 2026 to 22 November 2026 Participants must successfully complete the required modules by 22 November 2026 to become eligible to apply for the fellowship. Click HERE to enroll for a Pre-Fellowship training. Required Courses and Track Preparation Applicants must select one track and one sub-track for the cycle. The Internet Society does not permit participants to enroll in multiple tracks during the same cycle. Participants should therefore choose the sub-track that best matches their: Interests Experience Professional background Community needs Project idea Long-term goals The track-specific preparation ensures that the eventual fellowship project is grounded in the participant s area of interest and the Internet Society s mission. For example, a participant interested in community networks may consider the Community-Centered Connectivity sub-track, while someone working on Internet regulation or governance may find Internet Policy more relevant. Who Should Apply? The Internet Society describes its target fellows as people who combine local knowledge with broader awareness of Internet issues. The program particularly looks for individuals who are: Locally Rooted and Globally Aware Applicants should understand challenges affecting their own communities while being able to connect those challenges to broader Internet issues. These may include: Internet governance Connectivity Internet security Online trust and safety Digital inclusion Community development Action-Oriented The fellowship is intended for people who want to create practical change. Applicants should be able to demonstrate an interest in moving beyond purely academic or theoretical work toward: Projects Advocacy Training Community initiatives Technical interventions Policy engagement Collaborative Internet challenges often require collaboration across different sectors. The Internet Society therefore looks for people who can work with: Civil society Government Industry Technical communities Academic institutions Local communities Other stakeholders Strong Communicators Applicants should be able to explain complex technical, policy, or security issues in ways that different audiences can understand. Communication is particularly important for fellows working across sectors or attempting to influence policy and community behavior. Evidence-Based and Strategic Applicants should be capable of using evidence, data, analysis, and structured reasoning to identify challenges and opportunities. Committed to Long-Term Public Benefit The Internet Society is looking for people who view the fellowship as part of a longer-term commitment to strengthening an open, secure, trustworthy, and inclusive Internet. Application Requirements Completing the pre-fellowship training is only one requirement. Applicants must also meet several other conditions. 1. Completion of Required Training Applicants must complete all required Pre-Fellowship Training modules before they can apply. This is a mandatory prerequisite. 2. Project Plan During the training period, participants are expected to develop a realistic project plan aligned with the Internet Society s mission. The project must be achievable within the fellowship period. 3. English Proficiency Applicants must have a high level of reading, speaking, and writing proficiency in English . This requirement is relevant because the training, communication, application process, and fellowship activities require participants to work effectively in English. 4. Reliable Internet Access Applicants need continuous Internet access throughout the different phases of the program. They must also have the appropriate equipment needed to participate in: Online training Virtual meetings Fellowship sessions Project activities Other online program requirements 5. Weekly Time Commitment Participants must be available to take part in weekly sessions and dedicate a minimum of four hours per week during the 10-month fellowship program. Prospective applicants should therefore consider their existing employment, studies, professional commitments, and other responsibilities before applying. 6. Valid Passport Applicants must hold a valid passport that remains valid for at least six months beyond anticipated fellowship-related travel dates . This requirement is particularly important because selected fellows may receive travel support to participate in relevant Internet events. 7. Current Fellowship Status Applicants cannot be currently participating in a 2026 Internet Society fellowship . Is There a Nationality or Country Restriction? The current official Fellowship Program page describes the program as open to people interested in developing skills in Internet policy, community mobilization, connectivity, Internet safety, and security. The current program information does not state a specific nationality or country restriction. The Internet Society has also stated that it remains committed to geographic, gender, and age diversity in the redesigned program. Therefore, prospective applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, the Americas, the Middle East, Oceania, and other regions should consult the official application information rather than assuming that nationality is an automatic barrier. The program is global in orientation, but applicants must still satisfy all stated requirements and compete through the selection process. Is There an Age Requirement? The current official Fellowship Program information does not specify a fixed age limit. Instead, the Internet Society explicitly states that the redesigned program is intended to accommodate a range of experience levels, including: Early-career professionals Mid-career practitioners Experienced leaders The organization also states that it is committed to age diversity. This makes the current unified fellowship different from some of the Internet Society s earlier programs that were specifically structured around career stages. Application Timeline for the 2027 Fellowship The current cycle follows a clearly defined timeline. 23 September 2026 Pre-Fellowship Training enrollment opens. 23 September to 22 November 2026 Participants complete the required self-paced training and develop their project ideas. 22 November 2026 Deadline for completing the required Pre-Fellowship Training. 18 December 2026 Final deadline for Fellowship Program applications. Applications become available on a rolling basis once participants complete the required training. 21 December 2026 to 29 January 2027 Fellowship applications are reviewed and the selection process takes place. 19 February 2027 Fellowship notifications and acceptance. 22 February 2027 Fellowship kick-off and onboarding. 1 June to 30 November 2027 Mentored fellowship project execution. 3 December 2027 Final project delivery. Early December 2027 Graduation ceremony. Important Application Deadline There are effectively two important deadlines in the application journey. The first is the deadline for completing the required training: 22 November 2026 The second is the final fellowship application deadline: 18 December 2026 Participants should not confuse the two. Completing the training by 22 November is necessary because applicants cannot begin the fellowship application until the required training has been successfully completed. Once completion is confirmed, the Internet Society states that eligible participants receive the fellowship application link by email within 24 hours. How the Application Process Works The application journey consists of seven major steps. Step 1: Enroll in Pre-Fellowship Training Prospective applicants first enroll in the required training. Step 2: Complete the Required Modules Participants must complete the modules associated with their selected track and sub-track. Step 3: Receive the Fellowship Application Link Once training completion is confirmed, eligible participants receive the fellowship application link by email. Step 4: Submit the Fellowship Application Applicants complete the application and submit their project proposal. Step 5: Application Review and Selection Applications are assessed through a competitive selection process. Step 6: Receive Fellowship Outcome Successful applicants receive fellowship offers and acceptance information. Step 7: Begin the Fellowship Selected fellows participate in onboarding and begin the fellowship journey. How Fellows Are Selected Completion of the training does not automatically lead to fellowship selection. The Internet Society states that fellowship selection is competitive. Applications and projects are considered based on factors including: Relevance Feasibility Potential impact Alignment with the Internet Society s mission Applicant preparation Applicant ability to deliver the proposed project The organization also expects applicants to demonstrate that their proposed work can produce meaningful community impact. What Makes a Strong Fellowship Application? The Internet Society provides several recommendations for applicants. Define a Specific Problem Applicants should avoid presenting an overly broad Internet challenge without identifying a concrete problem they intend to address. The proposed project should explain: What the problem is Who is affected Why the problem matters What change the project intends to produce Present a Practical Solution The project should be realistic. Applicants should show that the proposed activities can actually be implemented during the fellowship period. Demonstrate Relevant Experience Applicants should provide evidence of previous work that demonstrates their ability to deliver. Relevant experience can come from: Advocacy Technical projects Community organizing Training Research Outreach Policy engagement Internet-related professional work Explain Community Connections Applicants should identify the communities they work with and explain why they are positioned to contribute to the proposed solution. Demonstrate Collaboration Applicants should explain how they have worked with other stakeholders and how collaboration could strengthen their project. Think Beyond the Fellowship Applicants should explain what happens after the fellowship ends. The Internet Society encourages applicants to demonstrate sustainability and explain how their work could continue through: Training Partnerships Networks Advocacy Further implementation Community engagement Connect the Project to the Internet Society s Mission The proposal should demonstrate a clear relationship with the Internet Society s objective of strengthening an open, globally connected, secure, and trustworthy Internet. Use of Artificial Intelligence in Applications The Internet Society has published specific guidance concerning generative AI. Applicants may use generative AI tools for supportive purposes such as: Brainstorming Language translation Grammar correction Accessibility support Structural editing However, the organization expects application essays and project proposals to reflect the applicant s own ideas, experience, insights, and project vision . The Internet Society warns that plagiarism or uncredited AI-generated narratives can result in disqualification. It also reserves the right to use algorithmic text verification systems. Applicants should therefore avoid submitting generic AI-generated statements that do not accurately represent their actual experience. Any application should be truthful, personal, and grounded in the applicant s real work and proposed project. What Happens If You Are Not Selected? Completing the training has value even if a participant is not ultimately selected as a fellow. According to the Internet Society s FAQ, trainees who complete the required training but are not selected can apply again in a future cycle without necessarily repeating training modules that remain current. They also retain ownership of their project plans and may continue developing them independently, seek other funding, or refine the idea for a future fellowship application. This means the training stage can function as a professional development and project-development experience in its own right. Can Applicants Build on Existing Projects? Yes. The Internet Society s FAQ states that applicants may build upon existing initiatives as long as the proposed fellowship project contains clearly defined: Objectives Activities Outcomes The proposed work must also be achievable within the fellowship period. This can be particularly useful for professionals who are already working on Internet-related projects but want to strengthen, expand, or formalize a particular component through the fellowship. Can Multiple Applicants Submit the Same Project? No. The Internet Society states that fellowship applications are assessed individually and each applicant is expected to submit their own project proposal. However, collaboration among fellows is encouraged where appropriate, especially where different projects address related challenges. Project Ownership Participants retain ownership of their project ideas. The Internet Society states that project plans remain the property of their creators and that participants may continue developing and implementing them independently regardless of whether they are selected for the fellowship. What Happens During the Fellowship? The fellowship combines structured learning, mentorship, practical implementation, and engagement with the wider Internet community. Throughout the program, fellows can expect to: Participate in foundational learning Engage in track-specific expert sessions Work with a dedicated mentor Develop and implement a practical project Participate in relevant Internet community events Report on project progress Produce tangible project outputs Connect with other Internet leaders The six-month project implementation period runs from 1 June to 30 November 2027 , followed by final project delivery in December 2027. Potential Project Outputs The Internet Society gives examples of the types of tangible outputs fellows may produce. These include: Policy briefs Research reports Training programs Community engagement initiatives Workshops Technical resources Implementation plans Awareness campaigns Toolkits Operational guides The specific output depends on the fellow s track, project category, objectives, and target community. Internet Society Fellowship Program and Career Development The fellowship is designed to support people at different stages of their professional journeys. The Internet Society specifically identifies: Emerging leaders Early-career professionals Mid-career practitioners Experienced Internet changemakers as part of the intended community. The program can therefore be relevant to people working in technical, policy, social, community, research, advocacy, and Internet governance roles, provided they can develop a project that aligns with the program s objectives. Global Community and Networking Internet challenges increasingly cross national boundaries. Connectivity, online safety, cybersecurity, Internet governance, digital inclusion, and community networks often involve stakeholders operating in multiple countries. The Fellowship Program therefore places emphasis on networking and cross-disciplinary collaboration. Fellows can interact with people working in different geographic regions and professional fields, helping create a broader community of people working toward an Internet that is open, secure, trustworthy, and globally connected. Travel and Internet Community Events The program includes opportunities for fellows to participate in relevant Internet events. The Internet Society identifies examples such as: Internet Governance Forum Africa Peering and Interconnection Forum NDSS Symposium Other program-relevant global or regional events The specific opportunities available to an individual fellow depend on their selected track and other program considerations. Frequently Asked Questions Is the Internet Society Fellowship fully funded? The program provides selected fellows with a project stipend of up to US$5,000 , subject to approval of the project budget, as well as travel support for a relevant global or regional Internet event. The official information does not describe the fellowship as a general full-cost-of-living scholarship, so applicants should not interpret the project stipend as a general personal living allowance. Is the pre-fellowship training free? The Internet Society describes the training and project-planning opportunity as open to everyone at no cost. Does completing the training guarantee a fellowship? No. Completing the required training makes a participant eligible to apply, but fellowship selection remains competitive. Can someone apply without completing the training? No. The required Pre-Fellowship Training must be completed before a participant can apply for the Fellowship Program. Can I choose more than one track? No. Participants may enroll in one track and one sub-track per cycle . Is there an age limit? The current Fellowship Program page does not specify a fixed age limit. The redesigned program explicitly welcomes early-career, mid-career, and experienced professionals. Is the program limited to a particular country? The current official Fellowship Program information does not state a specific nationality or country restriction. It presents the program as a global opportunity and emphasizes geographic diversity. Can I use AI to write my application? AI tools may be used for limited supportive purposes, but applicants are expected to submit their own ideas and authentic experiences. The Internet Society warns against plagiarism and uncredited AI-generated narratives. What happens if I complete the training but am not selected? You retain your project plan, can continue developing it independently, and may apply in a future cycle, subject to the applicable requirements. How to Apply for the Internet Society Fellowship Program The application pathway begins with the required Pre-Fellowship Training . Prospective applicants should: Visit the official Internet Society Fellowship Program page. Review the three available tracks and six sub-tracks. Select the track and sub-track that best match their interests, experience, and proposed project. Enroll in the required Pre-Fellowship Training. Complete all required modules by 22 November 2026 . Develop a realistic, locally grounded project plan during the training. Wait for confirmation of training completion and receipt of the fellowship application link. Complete and submit the fellowship application. Submit the application no later than 18 December 2026 . Monitor communications from the Internet Society during the selection period. The official program page provides access to the required training and application information. Official Fellowship Program: Internet Society Fellowship Program Pre-Fellowship Training: Enroll for Pre-Fellowship Training Fellowship FAQs: Internet Society Fellowship FAQs Key Dates at a Glance Stage Date Pre-Fellowship Training opens 23 September 2026 Training completion deadline 22 November 2026 Fellowship applications Rolling after training completion Final fellowship application deadline 18 December 2026 Application review and selection 21 December 2026–29 January 2027 Fellowship notifications 19 February 2027 Kick-off and onboarding 22 February 2027 Mentored project implementation 1 June–30 November 2027 Final project delivery 3 December 2027 Graduation Early December 2027 Pro Tip for Applicants Do not wait until December to begin thinking about your application. The fellowship application is the final stage of a process that begins with the Pre-Fellowship Training . Prospective applicants should enroll early, choose their track carefully, and use the training period to develop a specific project that addresses a clearly defined Internet challenge. A strong project should be practical rather than excessively broad. Clearly identify the problem, explain who is affected, describe the intervention, establish realistic objectives and outcomes, demonstrate your connection to the community, and explain how the work could continue after the fellowship. Applicants should also ensure that their proposal genuinely reflects their own experience and ideas, particularly given the Internet Society s policy on AI-assisted application writing. Visit HERE to learn more about the Internet Society Fellowship Program 2027 Conclusion The Internet Society Fellowship Program 2027 provides a structured pathway for Internet changemakers and emerging, mid-career, and experienced leaders to transform Internet-related ideas into practical projects with community impact. The redesigned 10-month program combines pre-fellowship training, specialized Internet learning, leadership development, mentorship, project funding, practical implementation, expert engagement, event participation, and global networking . Selected fellows can receive a project stipend of up to US$5,000 , subject to project-budget approval, travel support for a relevant global or regional Internet event, dedicated mentorship, and access to the Internet Society s wider leadership and alumni networks. The program covers three major areas: Internet Policy and Mobilization, Internet Connectivity, and Internet Safety and Security , with two specialized sub-tracks under each. This allows prospective fellows to align their training and project development with their particular interests and expertise. One of the most important features of the 2027 cycle is the compulsory training stage. Participants must complete the required Pre-Fellowship Training by 22 November 2026 before they become eligible to submit a fellowship application. Once eligible, they can apply on a rolling basis, with the final fellowship application deadline set for 18 December 2026 . The opportunity is presented as a global program without a stated nationality restriction, and the Internet Society has indicated its commitment to geographic, gender, and age diversity. The program welcomes people at different stages of their careers, provided they meet the requirements and can develop a feasible project aligned with the Internet Society s mission. For prospective applicants, the most important next step is therefore to begin with the training rather than waiting for the final application deadline. Completing the required courses, selecting the right sub-track, and developing a focused and realistic project plan can prepare applicants for the competitive fellowship application stage. Training completion deadline: 22 November 2026 Final Fellowship Application Deadline: 18 December 2026 Discover more Fellowship , Mentorship and Leadership Development opportunities on Opportunities for Youth (OFY). title: Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant 2026: $2,000 Grants for U.S. Organizations to Build Youth Leadership and Decision-Making Opportunities
summary: The Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant 2026 is a new funding opportunity from Youth Service America (YSA) , supported by an AmeriCorps MLK Day of Service grant , designed to help organizations create or strengthen formal structures through which young people can participate in leadership, decision-making, community service, and civic engagement. The grant will provide $2,000 to selected organizations that want to develop a new Youth Council or a similar youth leadership structure, or expand an existing one. In addition to establishing or strengthening youth leadership structures, grantees will be expected to organize a citywide, regional, or statewide Youth Leadership Summit around Martin Luther King Jr. Day and create continuing opportunities for youth voice, leadership, and decision-making through The Civic Season, from Juneteenth through July 4 . The program is particularly focused on ensuring that young people are not simply consulted occasionally but have meaningful opportunities to participate in organizational and community decision-making. YSA states that the grant program is intended to support the development or expansion of youth councils and similar structures while engaging at least 200 youth and adults in training or youth voice, leadership, and decision-making opportunities. Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant 2026: Overview Youth Service America is accepting applications from eligible U.S.-based organizations seeking funding to strengthen youth participation and leadership. The opportunity is connected to the MLK Day of Service , which will take place on January 18, 2027 . YSA s MLK Day of Service campaign describes the holiday as a national day of service focused on community action, service, and honoring the legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. For this particular grant, organizations will use the funding to create or expand structures that give young people a more formal role in organizational and community decision-making. Key details at a glance Opportunity: Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant Organizer: Youth Service America (YSA) Funding: AmeriCorps MLK Day of Service grant Grant amount: $2,000 per selected grantee Total funding available: $50,000 Number of organizations expected to receive grants: 25 Required local match: $1,000 in cash or in-kind support Minimum engagement requirement: 200 youth and adults Main focus: Youth voice, leadership, decision-making, youth councils, youth leadership structures, and community service MLK Day of Service: January 18, 2027 Application deadline: Sunday, October 25, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. local time Geographic eligibility: United States organizations meeting the program s organizational eligibility requirements Application format: Online application Contact: Mike Minks at mminks@ysa.org YSA s official MLK Day of Service page confirms that the program will award $2,000 grants, with $50,000 available overall and 25 citywide, regional, or statewide organizations expected to receive funding. What Is the Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant? The Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant is designed around the idea that young people should have meaningful opportunities to contribute to decisions affecting their organizations and communities. Rather than supporting only a one-time service event, the grant focuses on developing or expanding ongoing youth leadership structures . These can include Youth Councils or other formal youth leadership groups that allow young people to contribute ideas, participate in planning, advise organizations, and take part in decision-making processes. According to YSA, grant recipients will use the funding to support the development of new Youth Councils or similar youth leadership structures, or the expansion of existing ones . This makes the opportunity relevant to organizations that already have some youth engagement experience but want to create a more formal mechanism for youth participation, as well as organizations that are ready to establish a new youth leadership structure. What Will Grant Recipients Be Expected to Do? Receiving the $2,000 grant comes with specific expectations. Organizations should therefore consider whether they have the capacity to develop a youth leadership structure and sustain youth engagement beyond a single event. 1. Create or Expand a Youth Leadership Structure Applicants will need to describe their plans for establishing or strengthening a formal youth advisory or leadership board, council, or similar group. The application asks organizations to explain: Their current programs and organizational work. Their existing experience with youth engagement. Their experience with youth voice and leadership. Their experience involving young people in decision-making. Whether they plan to create a new youth advisory structure or expand an existing one. What they hope the youth leadership structure will accomplish. How youth participation could strengthen the organization. The emphasis is therefore not simply on recruiting young people for an event. Applicants are expected to demonstrate how youth leadership can become part of their organization s continuing work. 2. Organize a Youth Leadership Summit Around MLK Day Each grantee will be expected to organize a citywide or statewide Youth Leadership Summit on or around MLK Day . YSA indicates that the Summit should be organized with the organization s youth leadership group. The program is therefore designed to give young people an active role in shaping the event rather than having adults independently plan the entire experience. The Summit can be scheduled between January 11 and January 25, 2027 , although YSA says it should take place as close as possible to MLK Day on January 18, 2027 . The Summit should provide training connected to: Youth-adult partnerships Youth voice Youth leadership Community service project design Future youth-led service opportunities The 200-Person Engagement Requirement One of the most important requirements applicants need to understand is the minimum engagement target. Grant recipients are expected to engage at least 200 youth and adults through the Youth Leadership Summit and/or related youth voice, leadership, and decision-making opportunities. The application specifically requires applicants to acknowledge this requirement and provide an estimate of how many youth and adults they expect to engage in relevant training or opportunities. The goal is not simply to establish a small internal youth council. The youth leadership group should also help broaden youth participation and encourage other young people and adults to become involved. YSA describes the program as requiring grantees to organize a Youth Leadership Summit and ongoing opportunities through The Civic Season while engaging a minimum of 200 youth and adults in commitments to future or ongoing service and related training. Continuing Youth Engagement Through The Civic Season The Youth At Every Decision-Making Table initiative extends beyond MLK Day. Applicants are asked to explain how their youth leadership group could continue engaging other young people after the Summit during the remainder of the 2026–2027 academic year and through The Civic Season, from Juneteenth through July 4 . This means applicants should think about a longer-term engagement strategy rather than proposing a single event. Potential activities described in an application could include continued youth leadership meetings, peer engagement, youth-led service projects, community conversations, leadership training, youth advisory activities, or other forms of participation that are consistent with the organization s mission. The key consideration is that the youth leadership group should help create opportunities for its peers as well. Who Can Apply for the Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant? The application identifies several types of organizations as eligible. These include: K-12 schools Higher education institutions Out-of-school-time programs Afterschool programs Summer learning programs Positive youth development organizations Community-based organizations Faith-based organizations State governments Local governments YSA s official program information confirms these organizational categories as eligible for the Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grants. The application form also asks organizations to provide their organization name, organization type, contact information, mailing address, state, ZIP code, and website. Youth Representation and Inclusive Recruitment A major part of the application concerns how an organization will recruit young people who reflect the diversity of the community it serves. Applicants are asked to explain how they will recruit youth who are representative of their organization s or community s youth/student population. The application specifically identifies groups that applicants should consider reaching, including: Young people of color Young people from low-income families and neighborhoods Young people from rural areas Youth with disabilities Young people who are unhoused Young people in foster care Young people involved in the juvenile justice system Immigrants and refugees English Language Learners LGBTQ+ young people Young people from military families Other young people who are not typically asked to participate in leadership opportunities This component is important because the application is not simply asking organizations to create a youth council. Applicants must also explain how they will ensure that the council and related activities include young people whose perspectives may otherwise be overlooked. What Should Organizations Explain in Their Application? The application contains several substantive questions. Organizations should be prepared to address each area clearly and specifically. 1. Describe the Organization and Its Youth Engagement Experience Applicants must describe their organization, current programs, and previous experience with: Youth engagement Youth voice Youth leadership Youth decision-making This section provides an opportunity to demonstrate that the organization understands the needs of young people and has some capacity to work with them. 2. Explain the Youth Advisory or Leadership Structure Applicants must describe their plans and goals for creating or expanding a formal youth advisory board, leadership board, council, or similar group. The application asks organizations to explain: What they want to establish or expand. What they are excited about doing. What the youth group will contribute. How the planned actions will strengthen the organization. A strong response should therefore connect youth leadership directly to the organization s existing work rather than treating the youth group as a completely separate activity. 3. Explain How Youth Will Be Recruited Organizations must describe their recruitment strategy and explain how they will reach young people who represent the broader population they serve. This includes thinking about barriers that can prevent certain young people from participating and explaining how the organization will reach people who are traditionally underrepresented in leadership opportunities. 4. Describe the Youth Leadership Summit Applicants must provide preliminary ideas for a citywide or statewide Youth Leadership Summit taking place on or around MLK Day. The application emphasizes that the plans are preliminary because the event will ultimately be planned with the youth leadership group. Applicants should also explain how they intend to provide training to at least 200 youth and adults and encourage participants to commit to future or ongoing service. 5. Explain How Youth Will Engage Their Peers The application specifically asks organizations to consider what happens after the Summit. Applicants should provide ideas for how members of the youth leadership group can engage other young people throughout: The remainder of the 2026–2027 academic year The Civic Season from Juneteenth through July 4 This requirement reinforces the program s broader objective of expanding youth participation beyond a small leadership group. Grant Amount and Available Funding Each successful organization will receive a $2,000 grant . YSA states that $50,000 in total funding is available and that 25 citywide, regional, or statewide organizations will receive grants. The grant is funded through a federal AmeriCorps MLK Day of Service grant . Required $1,000 Match Funding Organizations applying for the grant must also be prepared to provide a $1,000 local match . The match can consist of: Cash contributions In-kind contributions Donated event supplies Food Recognition items for youth leadership group members or Summit participants Meeting space Event space Equipment Other qualifying local contributions Applicants must indicate whether they agree to meet the matching requirement and identify potential sources of the match. This means an organization applying for the $2,000 grant should consider how it will document an additional $1,000 in local support. What Can the $2,000 Grant Be Used For? The application asks applicants to submit a tentative $2,000 budget . A full budget will be submitted later if the organization is selected and enters into a grant agreement. However, the application clearly states that grant funds cannot be used for staff salaries and benefits . The funds also cannot be used for AmeriCorps-prohibited activities, including: Lobbying Partisan political activities Voter registration Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed budget is directly connected to allowable activities supporting youth leadership, youth voice, decision-making, training, and related program implementation. Application Deadline The deadline for the Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant is: Sunday, October 25, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. local time. YSA s official MLK Day of Service page confirms the October 25 deadline and specifies that the deadline is based on the applicant s local time. Organizations should not wait until the final day if they need time to develop their youth leadership plans, identify match funding, prepare the preliminary budget, and collect organizational information. How to Apply Applications are submitted through the Youth Service America online application. The application requires organizations to provide organizational and contact information and answer questions about their current programs, youth engagement experience, proposed youth leadership structure, recruitment strategy, Youth Leadership Summit, continuing engagement plans, anticipated participant numbers, budget, and match funding. The application also provides options to: Save progress and return later. Resume a previously saved application. Applicants with questions about the application can contact Mike Minks at mminks@ysa.org . Apply through the Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant application Important Note About AI and the Application The application itself contains a specific request that applicants not use AI to prepare their application responses . YSA says it wants to hear about the applicant organization and its own ideas in the organization s own words. It also states that it does not use AI to review applications. Applicants should therefore treat the application questions as an opportunity to describe their actual organization, existing youth engagement work, local community, proposed plans, and ideas rather than submitting generic or AI-generated responses. For this reason, organizations should make sure that their final application responses genuinely reflect their own experience and plans. MLK Day of Service and the Wider Program Context The Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant is part of YSA s broader MLK Day of Service programming. The next MLK Day of Service will take place on January 18, 2027 . YSA describes MLK Day as a federal holiday designated as a National Day of Service and encourages Americans to participate in service and community action. YSA s broader work focuses on helping young people find their voices, take action, develop civic skills, and contribute to their communities. The organization says its campaigns and events have engaged more than 3.2 million young people in service over the past decade. The Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant fits within this broader approach by emphasizing not only youth service but also youth voice, leadership, participation, and decision-making . Why the Youth Council Component Matters One of the distinctive features of this opportunity is its emphasis on establishing a formal youth leadership structure. A one-time event can create an opportunity for young people to participate on a particular day. A youth council or similar structure can provide an ongoing mechanism through which young people can: Share perspectives with organizational leaders. Help identify community needs. Participate in planning. Develop leadership skills. Help design service projects. Engage their peers. Build relationships with adult partners. Continue participating in decision-making beyond MLK Day. The grant therefore combines organizational development, youth leadership development, community service, and ongoing civic participation . Suggested Areas Organizations Should Think About Before Applying Although the application requires organizations to provide their own responses, prospective applicants may find it useful to think through several practical questions before beginning. Budget Consider how the $2,000 grant and $1,000 match could support allowable activities without being used for prohibited expenses.
